cards.front: Recall a key point about Tenses: Future and Conditional
cards.back: Grammar accuracy is essential for the writing and speaking papers, where it is worth up to 40% of marks. Always check cases, word order and verb endings.

cards.front: What should you know about german exam tips — tenses: future and conditional?
cards.back: 1. For Tenses: Future and Conditional, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Tenses: Future and Conditional, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
to become / will (e.g. Ich werde Arzt.)
future tense (e.g. Das Futur wird mit 'werden' gebildet.)

cards.front: What does der Konjunktiv II mean?
cards.back: conditional/subjunctive (e.g. Der Konjunktiv II drückt Wünsche aus.)
would + infinitive (e.g. Ich würde gern nach Italien reisen.)
if / when (e.g. Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause.)
would be (e.g. Wenn ich reich wäre...)
would have (e.g. Ich hätte gern ein neues Fahrrad.)
could (e.g. Ich könnte dir helfen, wenn ich Zeit hätte.)
would have to (e.g. Ich müsste mehr lernen.)

cards.front: What does die hypothetische Situation mean?
cards.back: hypothetical situation (e.g. Der Konjunktiv II beschreibt hypothetische Situationen.)

cards.front: What does der Wunsch (die Wünsche) mean?
cards.back: wish(es) (e.g. Ich hätte den Wunsch, nach Japan zu reisen.)

Students often forget word order in subordinate clauses. Wrong: Weil ich krank bin, ich bleibe zu Hause. Correct: Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause (in the MAIN clause after a subordinate clause, the verb comes FIRST, then the subject).
